findings.title: Migration crashes when `embed_category` was never set
findings.body:
The migration reads the existing category with `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` and does not check whether any row came back.

Site settings are only written to `site_settings` when changed from their default. `embed_category` defaulted to `''`, so on fresh installs and on most existing sites this query returns zero rows. Indexing row 0 of the empty `PG::Result` then raises, which aborts the migration.

The result is that upgrades, new installs and test DB setup all fail. Check that a row exists before reading `['id']`, and fall back to the uncategorized category otherwise.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are inserted raw, so previously valid configs stop matching
findings.body:
Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is inserted verbatim with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This skips the model's `before_validation` normalization.

The old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` accepted entries such as `http://eviltrout.com` and `https://example.com/1234`; the removed specs explicitly covered these. After migration those values are stored with scheme and path intact. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares them against the bare `uri.host`, so embedding silently stops working for those sites after upgrade.

The raw insert has other problems too:
- Blank lines insert empty-string hosts.
- `\r` from CRLF input is kept in the stored value.
- A value containing a single quote breaks the SQL statement.

Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank entries, and quote the values (or insert through the model).

findings.title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body:
`self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally. If `host` is nil, validation raises NoMethodError instead of failing with a validation error.

This happens in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` whenever the request has no `embeddable_host[host]` param, which turns a bad request into a 500. The client-side `cantSave` guard does not protect API callers.

Guard with `if host.present?`, or add `validates_presence_of :host`.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases only the column, and port-qualified hosts never match
findings.body:
`where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the argument. Ruby's `URI#host` does not downcase, so an embed URL such as `http://EvilTrout.com/x` (for example from TopicRetriever's raw `embed_url` param) never matches. Use `host.downcase`.

Separately, the format validation accepts an optional `:port`, so `example.com:8080` can be saved. The lookup compares only `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so such a record validates but can never authorize anything.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid hostnames
findings.body:
The regex requires a TLD of 2–5 letters (`\.[a-z]{2,5}`). This rejects many valid domains, such as `.museum`, `.travel`, `.software` and `.photography`, as well as `localhost` and IP addresses. The old `host_list` setting accepted all of these.

Admins cannot add such hosts through the new UI. Hosts migrated with these TLDs cannot be re-saved after editing.

findings.title: update/destroy crash with 500 on unknown id
findings.body:
`EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a nonexistent id. The next call, `save_host(host)` (line 11) or `host.destroy` (line 16), then raises NoMethodError.

The client gets a 500 instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` or raise `Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: `_ids` hydration crashes on null, keeps undefined entries, and always deletes the key
findings.body:
In the new plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError when the `_ids` value is null or not an array. Now that every `*_ids` key on a `__rest_serializer` payload is matched, that includes any non-association field that happens to end in `_ids`.

When the side-loaded collection is missing or an id is not found, the resulting array contains `undefined` entries. The original `_ids` key is deleted anyway, unlike the singular branch, which only replaces the key on success. The `|| []` is dead code because `map` always returns an array.

The net effect is that ids are lost and consumers receive arrays with holes.

findings.title: 'find embedded' test asks for fruit 2 but asserts fruit 1's data
findings.body:
The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the Pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`). Fruit 2 (banana) has `color_ids: [3]`.

The assertions that colors have length 2 with ids 1 and 2 only pass because the fake server ignores the id. The test does not verify what it appears to. Request id 1, or make the handler return the requested fruit.

findings.title: Spec name claims behavior that no longer exists
findings.body:
`expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for embeddable hosts at all. The spec "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and the unsaved topic has no embed.

Likewise, `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the 'with an emeddable host' block has no effect on the outcome. The spec misleads readers about the behavior: hosts are now irrelevant to expansion. It should be renamed or rewritten to cover the actual conditions.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped
findings.body:
`category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator. The new `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains all the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`).

This works because all fabricator files are loaded, but anyone looking for the category fabricators will look in the wrong file. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: No tests for the new admin create/update/destroy endpoints
